Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From b7880cb166ab62c2409046b2347261abf701530e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Matthew Wilcox (Oracle)" <willy@infradead.org>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 04:13:42 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] migrate: correct lock ordering for hugetlb file folios

Syzbot has found a deadlock (analyzed by Lance Yang):

1) Task (5749): Holds folio_lock, then tries to acquire i_mmap_rwsem(read lock).
2) Task (5754): Holds i_mmap_rwsem(write lock), then tries to acquire
folio_lock.

migrate_pages()
  -> migrate_hugetlbs()
    -> unmap_and_move_huge_page()     <- Takes folio_lock!
      -> remove_migration_ptes()
        -> __rmap_walk_file()
          -> i_mmap_lock_read()       <- Waits for i_mmap_rwsem(read lock)!

hugetlbfs_fallocate()
  -> hugetlbfs_punch_hole()           <- Takes i_mmap_rwsem(write lock)!
    -> hugetlbfs_zero_partial_page()
     -> filemap_lock_hugetlb_folio()
      -> filemap_lock_folio()
        -> __filemap_get_folio        <- Waits for folio_lock!

The migration path is the one taking locks in the wrong order according to
the documentation at the top of mm/rmap.c.  So expand the scope of the
existing i_mmap_lock to cover the calls to remove_migration_ptes() too.

This is (mostly) how it used to be after commit c0d0381ade79.  That was
removed by 336bf30eb765 for both file & anon hugetlb pages when it should
only have been removed for anon hugetlb pages.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20260109041345.3863089-2-willy@infradead.org
Signed-off-by: Matthew Wilcox (Oracle) <willy@infradead.org>
Fixes: 336bf30eb765 ("hugetlbfs: fix anon huge page migration race")
Reported-by: syzbot+2d9c96466c978346b55f@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/68e9715a.050a0220.1186a4.000d.GAE@google.com
Debugged-by: Lance Yang <lance.yang@linux.dev>
Acked-by: David Hildenbrand (Red Hat) <david@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>
Cc: Alistair Popple <apopple@nvidia.com>
Cc: Byungchul Park <byungchul@sk.com>
Cc: Gregory Price <gourry@gourry.net>
Cc: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>

Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/migrate.c b/mm/migrate.c
index 5169f9717f60..4688b9e38cd2 100644
--- a/mm/migrate.c
+++ b/mm/migrate.c
@@ -1458,6 +1458,7 @@ static int unmap_and_move_huge_page(new_folio_t get_new_folio,
 	int page_was_mapped = 0;
 	struct anon_vma *anon_vma = NULL;
 	struct address_space *mapping = NULL;
+	enum ttu_flags ttu = 0;
 
 	if (folio_ref_count(src) == 1) {
 		/* page was freed from under us. So we are done. */
@@ -1498,8 +1499,6 @@ static int unmap_and_move_huge_page(new_folio_t get_new_folio,
 		goto put_anon;
 
 	if (folio_mapped(src)) {
-		enum ttu_flags ttu = 0;
-
 		if (!folio_test_anon(src)) {
 			/*
 			 * In shared mappings, try_to_unmap could potentially
@@ -1516,16 +1515,17 @@ static int unmap_and_move_huge_page(new_folio_t get_new_folio,
 
 		try_to_migrate(src, ttu);
 		page_was_mapped = 1;
-
-		if (ttu & TTU_RMAP_LOCKED)
-			i_mmap_unlock_write(mapping);
 	}
 
 	if (!folio_mapped(src))
 		rc = move_to_new_folio(dst, src, mode);
 
 	if (page_was_mapped)
-		remove_migration_ptes(src, !rc ? dst : src, 0);
+		remove_migration_ptes(src, !rc ? dst : src,
+				ttu ? RMP_LOCKED : 0);
+
+	if (ttu & TTU_RMAP_LOCKED)
+		i_mmap_unlock_write(mapping);
 
 unlock_put_anon:
 	folio_unlock(dst);
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of the Patch

This patch fixes a deadlock in the hugetlb migration path by correcting the lock ordering between `folio_lock` and the `i_mmap_rwsem`. The deadlock occurred when one thread held `folio_lock` and waited for `i_mmap_rwsem` (read), while another thread held `i_mmap_rwsem` (write) and waited for `folio_lock`. The fix expands the scope of the `i_mmap_rwsem` write lock to cover both `try_to_migrate()` and `remove_migration_ptes()`, ensuring the proper lock ordering.

### Modifications in `mm/migrate.c`

1. **Variable declaration moved and made persistent**  
   - `enum ttu_flags ttu = 0;` is now declared at the beginning of `unmap_and_move_huge_page()` (line 1461), outside the `if (folio_mapped(src))` block.  
   - The previous local declaration inside that block (line 1501) is removed, making `ttu` accessible after the block ends.

2. **Lock holding extended over `remove_migration_ptes()`**  
   - After calling `try_to_migrate(src, ttu)`, the immediate `i_mmap_unlock_write(mapping)` when `TTU_RMAP_LOCKED` was set (old lines 1518–1519) is removed.  
   - The call to `remove_migration_ptes()` now uses `ttu ? RMP_LOCKED : 0` as the third argument instead of the constant `0`. This passes the `RMP_LOCKED` flag when the rmap was already locked (i.e., for shared/file hugetlb folios).  
   - After `remove_migration_ptes()`, a new `if (ttu & TTU_RMAP_LOCKED) i_mmap_unlock_write(mapping)` is added (after line 1521), ensuring the write lock is released only after both operations complete.

### Relationship Between the Modifications

- The core logic change is **locking the i_mmap_rwsem write lock across two critical sections** that both operate on the page table entries: `try_to_migrate()` and `remove_migration_ptes()`. Previously, the lock was dropped right after `try_to_migrate()`, exposing a window where `remove_migration_ptes()` could run without the lock. This caused the deadlock when another thread acquired `i_mmap_rwsem` write and waited for `folio_lock`.

- Moving the declaration of `ttu` and the unlock call ensures:
  - The `ttu` variable persists beyond the `if (folio_mapped(src))` block, so its value (whether `TTU_RMAP_LOCKED` was set) can be used later in `remove_migration_ptes()` and to decide whether to unlock.
  - The unlock happens **after** `remove_migration_ptes()` is called, maintaining the lock across both operations for file-backed hugetlb folios.

- This restores the behavior from commit `c0d0381ade79`, which was mistakenly removed by `336bf30eb765` for anon pages as well. The fix correctly limits the extended locking to file hugetlb pages (where `TTU_RMAP_LOCKED` is set) since anon pages do not require the rmap lock for `remove_migration_ptes()`.

**In summary**, the patch adjusts the lock acquisition and release order within `unmap_and_move_huge_page()` to prevent a deadlock by holding the i_mmap_rwsem write lock over both the unmap and the migration PTE cleanup steps for shared hugetlb mappings.
